@about: The Piping add-on's words (pipe design). Pipe-fitters' terms: run, nominal size (NPS), DN, schedule, type K/L/M, elbow, tee, wye, reducer, valve, invert, slope, P&ID.
pipe.name: Pipe run
symbol.name: Schematic symbol
table.name: Pipe schedule
table.title: Pipe schedule
solid.name: Pipe {tag}
cmd.pipe.help: Draw a pipe run on its centerline: choose the material, class and nominal size; elbows, reducers and tees come by themselves
cmd.valve.help: Put valves, strainers, flanges and unions on pipe runs (or take them off)
cmd.pidsym.help: Place schematic symbols: valves, a pump, a relief valve, instrument balloons, flow arrows
cmd.pipesched.help: The pipe and fitting schedule, placed as a table that keeps itself up to date
cmd.pipe3d.help: Build the solids of every pipe run on the 3D tab again
ask.pipe.first: First point of the pipe run ({size}); start on a pipe to branch from it
ask.pipe.next: Next point ({size}); end on a pipe to connect to it
ask.slope.in: Slope, inches per foot (1/4, 1/8, 0 for level)
ask.valve: Click a pipe where the {type} goes
ask.valve.remove: Click the valve to take off
ask.table: Where the schedule goes (its top left corner)
done.table: Schedule placed. It follows the pipes as they change.
done.3d: Solids built again for {n} pipe runs.
done.3d.off: Solids are switched off in Settings › CadCraft › Piping.
warn.slope: A drain flatter than the plumbing code's least slope for its size ({need}).
warn.flat: A level drain: the plumbing code asks at least {need} for its size.
warn.short: A section is too short for its fittings: they overlap.
warn.hairpin: The run turns back on itself at a corner: no elbow can be drawn there.
warn.maxpts: A run holds up to 100 points: this one ends here. Start a new run from its end.
err.size: That size is not made in {mat}.
err.slope: That is not a slope: type inches per foot (1/4) or a percent (2%).
err.run: That run cannot be drawn: it needs two different points.
err.nopipes: There are no pipe runs in the drawing.
export.takeoff: Pipes for TakeoffCraft (PDF with the takeoff inside)
pack.name: Pipes in {name}
pack.description: The pipe, fitting and valve items of one CadCraft drawing; steel pipe with its weight. No rates: set your own.
pack.assume.pipe: Length is center to center through the fittings, along the slope; steel weight is the plain-end weight per ASME B36.10M.
pack.assume.count: One per fitting or valve in the drawing; joints (welds, solder, solvent) are not counted.
pack.source.drawn: Lengths measured on the drawing, center to center through the fittings
panel.none: No pipe runs yet: type PIPE.
cmd.pipenet.help: Water supply from a source point: flow, velocity and pressure lost to each fixture from the fixture units you give (PNET)
net.source: Source: click on the end of a pipe run where the supply comes in [Pressure/Reset fixtures]
net.reset: The fixtures you named were forgotten.
net.avail: Supply pressure at the source in kPa (0 = not given)
net.min: Pressure needed at a fixture in kPa (0 = not given)
net.pressure.set: Supply {a} kPa, needed at a fixture {m} kPa.
net.fixture: Fixture at the end {tag} ({x}, {y}): {list}, or a number of fixture units (0 = none)
net.err.source: The point is not on the end of a pipe run. Click the end where the supply comes in.
net.err.nopipes: There are no pipe runs in this drawing.
net.err.noends: No free pipe ends were found, so there is nowhere for the water to go.
net.err.nosrc: Run PIPENET first and click the source, then export.
net.note.nofixture: The end {tag} {key} has no fixture, so it takes no water.
net.note.loop: {n} pipe loops were found. The calculation follows a tree, so loops are ignored.
net.note.unreached: {n} pipe sections are not joined to the source.
net.head: {n} fixtures. The furthest in pressure terms: {worst}.
net.sizes: {n} runs are too small for their flow (fast) or much bigger than needed: {list}.
net.beyond: Some demand is beyond the end of the demand curve. Type the curve of your code to go further.
net.defaults: Demand uses a labelled default curve and the fitting losses are rounded defaults. Check with your engineer before you rely on them.
